title: UPDATE: Rime Shuts Down Prism AI Voice Model Shortly After Debut
summary:
The AI voice tool developed by Rime is no longer available for use, ending its brief public launch period. The speech-to-speech model, known as Prism, was deactivated on Oct. 30 just two days after the startup debuted the technology to the public.

Rime had marketed Prism as a secure solution for the banking and regulatory sectors because the model creates a text transcript of its replies before speaking them, allowing users to monitor or block content mid-call. Backed by $35M in funding, the company claimed the tool's 300ms response time was four times faster than GPT-Live from OpenAI.

selectedTweets.text:
Rime has launched Prism, its new speech-to-speech model for AI voice agents that writes each reply as text before saying it out loud.

Companies can edit the transcript and block anything the agent shouldn't say, while Prism keeps the call going and looks up an account or freezes a card mid-conversation.

Rime says no other speech-to-speech model works this way, which makes Prism a safer fit for banks and other regulated businesses.
